fieldMarks: Male black all over with shiny purple gloss
Much like Brown-headed Cowbird in size and shape; females not safely identified
Most other all-black birds are either much larger or have pale eyes
behavior: Migration within North America poorly known; spring numbers move through southern Florida, and strays have reached Texas, Oklahoma and Maine
Forages mostly walking on the ground in open areas, often in small flocks with other cowbirds or blackbirds
Melodious warble song and harsh metallic call notes
habitat: Semi-open country; in North America mostly near the coast, often foraging on extensive lawns.
range: Resident from eastern Panama south to central Chile and Argentina; expanded through the Caribbean during the 1900s, reaching Puerto Rico in 1955; in North America occurs mostly in southern Florida.

lookalikes.name: Brown-headed cowbird
lookalikes.howToTell: Similar in size and shape; the male Shiny is entirely black with purple gloss, and females are not safely separated.
